gaps.text: In-line measurement of cell density (or optical density) with the existing cell count or optical density measurement
In-line measurement of temperature with a temperature sensor on the bioreactor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of Raman and UV-Vis ATR spectra taken at the same probe spot into one matrix, with per-block scaling so neither block dominates. Both blocks keep their own calibration and their own drift checks, and their different acquisition rates must be aligned to a common time step. The fused model must beat the best single Raman model on held-out runs, otherwise the extra channel is dropped.)
No supplied source gives accuracy, detection limits or response times for glucose and lactate in cell-culture medium.

items.finding: The source varied temperature, along with acid concentrations and ionic strength, to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This could prompt testing whether the calibration remains robust across bioreactor temperature excursions and whether temperature is logged as a model input.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: It does not describe an in-line temperature sensor or a bioreactor; it is a lithium-recycling extraction study.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E02 ¶19

items.finding: For a continuous process at a fixed probe location, the source says calibrations can be narrower and validation can use independent steady-state runs, with online monitoring focused on drift and out-of-specification detection.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform how a fused Raman/UV-Vis model is validated on held-out runs and how drift checks are framed, but it does not describe data fusion itself.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns FT-IR/Raman monitoring in lithium recycling, not Raman/UV-Vis ATR in cell-culture medium; per-block scaling and acquisition-rate alignment are not addressed.

citation.quote: In contrast, a continuous process at a fixed probe location is intended to operate in a steady-state window, which simplifies the model design: calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, validation can rely on independent steady-state runs, and online monitoring focuses on drift and out-of-specification detection rather than resolving the rapidly changing composition.
citation.label: E02 ¶8

items.finding: The source notes that in-line method drawbacks such as calibration maintenance and sensor drift/aging can be addressed by checking the baseline in pure-component phases and monitoring drift.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform separate drift checks for each spectral block, for example baseline checks during known process phases, before deciding whether the fused model beats the best single Raman model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a lithium-recycling liquid-liquid extraction study, not cell culture, and it does not discuss Raman/UV-Vis fusion or per-block scaling.

citation.quote: Potential typical drawbacks of any in-line method are maintenance efforts like calibration, and actions to sensor drift and aging could be easily overcome by checking the baseline in each cycle of pure component phases of process operation and monitoring any drift in order to be able to react.
citation.label: E02 ¶72
